jobs.occupation: Marie Skłodowska-Curie PhD fellowship in Learning and Optimization Algorithms for Carbon-Aware Datacenter Fleets - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
A Marie Skłodowska-Curie PhD fellowship is available in the Embedded Systems Engineering (ESE) section at DTU Compute. You will be one of the 15 Doctoral Candidates (DCs) of the MSCA Doctoral Network AEGIS, Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets, which Prof. Paul Pop, DTU, coordinates together with 10 partners across Europe.

This is a software and algorithms project. You will design algorithms and build software that decide where AI workloads run and when datacenter sites change their power use, so that hundreds of separate sites act as one carbon-efficient grid resource. The project does not involve electronics, FPGAs, or low-level embedded development, and it does not require prior knowledge of datacenters or energy systems: with a strong background in algorithms and data structures, you can learn the optimization methods and the domain during the PhD.

Marie Skłodowska-Curie fellowships are among the most respected and best-paid PhD positions in Europe. AEGIS sits where two fast-growing fields meet: datacenters and AI infrastructure on one side, energy and power systems on the other. Few people can work across both, so the skills you build here are scarce and in high demand. Our graduates will be ready for roles at cloud and datacenter operators, energy companies, grid operators, telecom companies, and in academia.

As an MSCA Doctoral Candidate, you will receive: (i) a competitive salary and employment conditions in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement and MSCA rules; (ii) two funded secondments, at TU Berlin and at Center Denmark; and (iii) a network-wide training program. The MSCA mobility and, where applicable, family contributions form part of the total employment remuneration and are not necessarily paid as separate supplements.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project is DC13, Fleet-Level Workload Shaping with Live Grid Signals. You will build the central orchestration engine of the AEGIS fleet: reacting to live grid signals, it decides where to place, pause, or move workloads, and which sites should change their power use with batteries, cooling, and adaptable compute. You will be responsible for:

• Designing a multi-agent orchestrator that can handle multiple datacenter sites.
• Implementing multi-timescale control, from sub-second to hourly decisions.
• Developing learning-based decision methods, such as contextual bandits with bounded-regret guarantees.
• Building a counterfactual analysis toolkit that estimates the carbon savings of different orchestration policies.
• Publishing and disseminating research in international conferences and journals.
• Collaborating with the academic and industrial partners in AEGIS, and contributing to the department with service work, including being a Teaching Assistant.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

We expect that you have:

• Strong algorithms and data structures, and solid programming skills.
• A background in one or more of: machine learning, reinforcement learning, combinatorial optimization, operations research, or distributed systems.
• Curiosity, initiative, and the drive to own a problem end to end.
• Good spoken and written English.
The standard MSCA eligibility criteria also apply:

• No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment you must not yet hold a PhD.
• Mobility rule. You must not have lived or done your main activity (work or studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months just before you are recruited. Short stays such as holidays do not count.
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of applicants will be based on academic qualifications, strength in algorithms and programming, motivation and initiative, and fit with the research area. The assessment will be carried out by an academic assessment committee.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is full-time.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Prof. Paul Pop (paupo@dtu.dk). You can read more about the AEGIS network at aegis-dn.eu, the DC13 project page at aegis-dn.eu/positions/dc13, DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk, and about Paul Pop. More details on relevant research problems are available from Paul Pop's Google Scholar page.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• An example text written by you, such as a thesis chapter, report, paper, or substantial technical documentation
• An example code sample written by you, or a repository link with a short explanation of your contribution
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Embedded Systems Engineering (ESE) is one of the research sections at DTU Compute. We develop methods and tools for distributed embedded and cyber-physical systems, with emphasis on timing, safety, dependability, optimization, and real-time communication. DTU Compute spans mathematics, statistics, computer science, and engineering.

DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: L&S Category Specialist - Material Handling Equipment Procurement
jobs.description:
Please note: This is a full-time office-based role (5 days/week)

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark

Opportunity

Are you curious, driven by impact, and excited by the idea of shaping how a global logistics leader manages its assets in the AI era?

We are looking for a Category Specialist to join our Material Handling Equipment (MHE) category team at a pivotal moment: Maersk is building an AI-powered asset platform (AssetIQ) that is transforming how we plan, source, and manage assets across their full lifecycle.

In this role, you will bring your live, real-world category and supplier experience directly into that transformation — partnering closely with the product team behind our new AI-guided workflows to solve real category problems without delay, so our processes develop, scale, and deliver Procurement and Asset Management Excellence from day one.

Alongside this, you will support and drive core category work — sourcing, supplier performance, and asset lifecycle optimization for our global MHE fleet — translating data and insight into decisions that create measurable value across our operations.

What We Offer

At Maersk, you will join a global team responsible for a strategically important category with significant spend and business impact — and you will do so at a moment when the category itself is being reinvented. You will work hand-in-hand with our inhouse platform development team as their category partner, helping shape live, AI-guided processes rather than inheriting a finished system. Alongside this, you will gain exposure to global stakeholders, supplier negotiations, category strategy development, and operational improvement initiatives, building deep expertise in logistics, material handling equipment, and AI-enabled asset management.

Category Management & Procurement

• Support and drive execution of category strategies for Material Handling Equipment (MHE).

• Coordinate sourcing activities including RFQs, tenders, negotiations, and contracting.

• Collaborate with regional procurement teams to consolidate demand and maximize value creation.

• Support supplier relationship management and performance improvement initiatives.

• Contribute to commercial discussions and negotiations with key suppliers.

Data, AI & Business Excellence

• Analyze spend, supplier, contract, and asset data — using our AI-powered asset platform — to identify optimization opportunities.

• Surface and personally resolve real category and supplier challenges from sourcing and asset management, turning your hands-on expertise into streamlined data enabled workflows.

• Take new AI-guided processes from concept to category-wide standard: co-creating workflows with the digital team, pressure-testing them in live sourcing situations, and scaling what works.

• Support and drive reporting, category performance tracking, and business case development.

Who We Are Looking For

• Experience within logistics, procurement, category management, supply chain, warehousing operations, or a related field.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively across business and supplier teams.

• Applied analytical skills and the ability to translate data into business insights.

• Commercial mindset with an understanding of supplier management and negotiations.

• Genuinely passionate about how AI and digital platforms can transform established ways of working.

• Curious, proactive, and motivated to drive improvements and challenge the status quo.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Engineering, Business, Economics, or a related field.

• Experience within logistics, warehousing, or handling equipment environments.

• Exposure to sourcing, category management, supplier relationship management, or procurement analytics.

• Familiarity with Agentic AI Platforms, procurement systems, reporting tools, or data analysis platforms.

Success in This Role

You will thrive in this role if you are intrinsically motivated by impact — energized by combining procurement, stakeholder engagement, analytics, and problem-solving to create meaningful business value, and genuinely curious about how AI can reshape the way we work. You are comfortable working across functions, building strong supplier and stakeholder relationships, and partnering with our AssetIQ team to turn real category challenges into scalable digital solutions — helping to lift Procurement and Asset Management Excellence at Maersk to the next level.

Join us and help shape how we source, manage, and optimize assets at Maersk — where category expertise meets AI-driven transformation.

Maersk is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we embrace different styles of thinking. Maersk is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applicants without regard to race, colour, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy or parental leave, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with all legal requirements.

We are happy to support your need for any adjustments during the application and hiring process. If you need special assistance or an accommodation to use our website, apply for a position, or to perform a job, please contact us by emailing accommodationrequests@maersk.com.

A broad and highly visible P&O role at the heart of Xellia’s global organization

Are you an experienced P&O professional who combines strong business understanding with a pragmatic yet ambitious approach and the ability to get things done?

Xellia Pharmaceuticals is looking for a Senior Business Partner P&O to take on a broad and highly visible role at our Copenhagen headquarters. You will work across both strategic and operational P&O priorities and play an important role in translating Xellia’s strategy into organizational capability, strong leadership practices and pragmatic P&O solutions.

This is a role for someone who enjoys operating in a fast-paced, ambitious and performance-driven international environment. You will interact with senior leaders and executives across the organization and take ownership of several important global P&O processes while remaining close to the day-to-day execution.

In other words, this is not a role where strategy and execution are separated. You will get the opportunity to do both.

Your role

As Senior Business Partner P&O, you will become part of Xellia’s global People & Organization function and work from our headquarters in Copenhagen.

You will act as a trusted sparring partner to senior leaders while taking direct ownership of a broad portfolio of P&O activities. A significant part of your role will be to ensure that processes are not only designed, but implemented, followed through and continuously improved.

Talent Acquisition will be an important part of your role. You will manage selected senior and strategically important recruitments across the organization, covering the process from talent attraction and sourcing through assessment, selection and offer. In addition, you will provide hands-on Talent Acquisition support to the Copenhagen site when needed and contribute to continuously strengthening Xellia’s approach to recruitment and talent attraction.

Your broader responsibilities will include:

• Driving selected global organizational review processes, including succession planning, organizational assessments and input to workforce and capability planning

• Driving the global performance management cycle and supporting leaders on performance-related matters

• Acting as a trusted P&O partner to leaders and providing pragmatic, business-oriented advice

• Driving and developing learning and development initiatives, including implementation of Xellia’s global competency framework

• Supporting leadership development and coordinating relevant leadership training and coaching initiatives

• Contributing to employee engagement activities, including analysis, action planning and follow-up

• Supporting employer branding activities in Copenhagen

• Managing external recruitment, assessment and development partners and ensuring both quality and commercial relevance

• Leading and contributing to global and local P&O projects and new initiatives

You will also play an active role in developing how Xellia uses AI and technology within P&O. This already includes AI-supported tools for job descriptions, job advertisements and structured interview guides, and we expect you to help identify further opportunities where technology can improve quality, speed and the employee and manager experience.

The formal scope spans strategic and operational P&O support, talent acquisition, performance management, organizational development, leadership development and vendor management. We do not expect you to be a unicorn who has mastered every aspect of P&O. We are looking for a passionate and committed professional who sees the opportunity in a broad portfolio of responsibilities and is motivated by taking ownership, creating momentum and successfully juggling the many different priorities the role entails.

Who are you?

We expect you to have a solid background from a senior HR role, ideally from an international and commercially oriented organization where expectations, pace and stakeholder complexity are high.

You probably bring:

• Strong experience within Talent Acquisition, preferably including senior and strategically important recruitments, combined with experience across several broader HR disciplines

• Experience driving organizational processes such as organizational reviews, succession planning, performance management or workforce planning

• Experience working directly with senior leaders and the confidence to challenge constructively when needed

• A strong business mindset and an ability to translate organizational needs into pragmatic solutions

• Experience managing projects and processes across functions and geographies

• An interest in how AI, data and technology can strengthen HR/P&O

• Strong communication skills and professional fluency in English

Experience from pharmaceuticals, life sciences or another highly regulated industry can be an advantage, but is not a prerequisite.

More importantly, you understand what it takes to operate successfully in an international corporate environment with high expectations for quality, responsiveness and execution.

The person we are looking for

Your way of working will be just as important as your HR toolbox.

You are quick-thinking, resourceful and action-oriented, and you naturally create momentum around the activities you own. You are comfortable moving between senior stakeholder discussions and very practical execution – sometimes within the same hour.

You have the maturity and robustness to navigate different perspectives and senior stakeholders in an international organization, and you communicate clearly and confidently.

At the same time, you have a strong hands-on mentality. You take ownership, follow through and do not consider operational tasks beneath your level. You thrive in a role where the breadth is significant, priorities can shift quickly, and delivering high-quality support to the business matters.

A bit about us

Xellia is a 120-year-old company with a refreshingly start-up feel inside. We have spent more than a century at the forefront of anti-infective medicine, making a difference to patients all over the world – and we are just as ambitious today as we were a hundred years ago.

We have recently refreshed our brand around a simple, human idea: We’re Your People. It is built on the strong relationships and trusted partnerships that have always defined Xellia, putting the real Xellians – the warm, expert and dedicated people behind the science – front and center.

Why Xellia?

Because you will be joining at a genuinely exciting moment – with a refreshed brand, real momentum and the rare combination of a 120-year heritage with start-up energy inside. The work matters. The medicines we make help patients in some of the most critical moments of their lives.

For the right person, this role offers a compelling combination of seniority, breadth, international exposure and hands-on responsibility. You will have the opportunity to influence important global P&O processes, work closely with senior stakeholders and help develop how Xellia approaches talent, performance, organizational capability and the use of new technology within P&O.

And because here, you are not just a hire – you are one of us.

We’re Your People. Come and be one of them.

Practical information

The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark. Workplace presence is expected approximately four days per week, and occasional travel may be required.

Contact and application

The recruitment process is handled by European Search Company on behalf of Xellia Pharmaceuticals. All inquiries are treated confidentially.

For additional information about the position, please contact Christoffer Bjørk Petersen on +45 20 80 16 38 or Brian Ranvits on +45 20 48 05 48.

If you see yourself in the position, please send your application by using the Apply button below.

Apply

Software Developer and Consultant for Life Science & Pharma Industry

About DAQUMA

In the summer of 2022, Bjarke, Peter and Sille started a new consultancy supporting life science companies with various elements of IT implementation. DAQUMA is a Technology and Data solution provider that helps life science companies succeed through implementations, data migrations, data integration, data management and quality control.

We believe in flexibility, flat hierarchies, and the freedom to shape both DAQUMA’s journey and your own professional path.

About the role

We are looking for a Software Developer and Consultant to support our Life Science and Pharma clients with the implementation and integration of our platform, DAQUMA:AI.

DAQUMA:AI is built on Microsoft Azure Services, and your role will primarily focus on integrating our platform into clients’ existing enterprise and regulated IT environments.

This is a client-facing consulting role where you will work directly with stakeholders to implement integrations, support deployment activities, and contribute to the technical implementation of our software.

You will:

• Collaborate with clients to understand their IT landscape, workflows, and integration needs.

• Implement and configure IT solutions based on client specifications.

• Design and implement integrations using Azure-native services such as API Management, Logic Apps, and App Services.

• Support the deployment of AI-driven document and data processing solutions.

• Maintain documentation of system configurations, integrations, and mappings.

• Troubleshoot technical issues and provide technical support.

• Conduct onboarding sessions and workshops for clients on DAQUMA:AI.

• Ensure integrations comply with requirements in regulated environments (e.g., GxP).

• Connect and harmonize data across enterprise systems such as Veeva Vault.

• Deliver on and support migration projects and other implementation projects for clients.

About you

You bring:

• A strong consulting mindset and a passion for delivering impactful client solutions.

• Hands-on experience working with the Microsoft Azure cloud platform.

• Experience with system and API integrations in enterprise environments.

• Experience in client-facing implementation or consulting roles.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to engage with both business and IT stakeholders.

• The ability to work independently as well as in collaborative teams.

Experience in one or more of the following areas is a plus:

• Life Science / Pharma industry experience.

• Experience in regulated environments (e.g., GxP).

• Veeva Vault experience.

• Previous consultancy experience.

• Relevant Azure certifications such as AZ204, AZ305, or AI102 are considered a plus; however, proven hands-on implementation experience is prioritized over certifications.

Location

On-site at our office in Nordvest, Copenhagen. Hybrid work flexibility is possible, and travel to client offices may be required.

What we offer

At DAQUMA, our team is what makes the difference. We invest in your growth through:

• A competitive salary and compensation package.

• A dedicated mentor to support your professional development.

• Exciting engagements within the Life Science and Pharma sectors.

• Continuous learning with a dedicated training budget.

• A dynamic scale-up culture where you can actively shape the company.

Formalities

If you want to join this exciting venture and help our clients reach their goals, please submit your CV by uploading it here on our website or emailing it to recruitment@daquma.com.

Find us on LinkedIn.

PostDoc in aerobiological modelling
Are you interested in atmospheric science and can you contribute to the development of a new generation of numerical models describing concentrations and transport of bioaerosols? Then the Department of Environmental Science invites you to apply for a 2 year post doc position, with possibility for extension. The position is associated with two research projects funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation: 1) NNF RECRUIT, 2022-2029 and NNF EARLY-BLIGHT, 2026-2029. The position is associated with two research projects funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation: 1) NNF RECRUIT, 2022-2029 and NNF EARLY-BLIGHT, 2026-2029.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2 year position from 1 March 2027 or as soon possible. This is a fixed-term position to end on 28 February 2029, but with possibility for an extension.

Job description
• You will be contributing to further development of the WRF-Chem model to handle a large range of bioaerosols in particular pollen and fungal spores. The geographical focus is on both the urban environment and agricultural areas in Denmark
• You will be contributing to the dynamical integration of near real-time data into WRF-Chem 
• You will be contributing to the development of machine learning models used on data from Poleno Jupiters, applying Python and machine learning.
• The position will focus on implementing grass pollen (both generic grasses and specific grass species) and selected fungal spores such as Alternaria alternata and Phytophtora infestans
• You will work with data obtained with Poleno Jupiter instruments, with data obtained with DNA methods and data obtained with a Hirst trap. 
• Numerical models used by the group covers the particle dispersion model HYSPLIT in combination and the numerical models WRF and WRF-Chem
• You will be working in an aerobiological research group funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation containing two additional post docs, a PhD student and a professor. This teams covers expertise on numerical modelling, atmosphere, microbiology and bioinformatics
• These activities will be in close collaboration with a group of technicians
• Disseminate results is a key aspect, which involves the production of manuscripts, both as co-author and lead author, for international peer-reviewed publications and participation in relevant conferences.
Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in environmental science, physics, chemistry, mathematics, engineering or similar. You need to demonstrate experience with collaboration and presenting works at international conferences and leading manuscripts published in international peer reviewed journals. Understanding of the atmosphere and its modelling is essential.

• Model development of WRF-Chem is complex. Documented experience using FORTRAN, C or similar is therefore required
• A substantial fraction of the technical part will be handled on high performance computers and the AI supercomputer GEFION, all operated in a Linux Environment. Documented experience with Linux is therefore also required
• Candidates with a completed PhD degree before the interview date will also be considered 
• Documented research experience on numerical modelling
• Experience with either WRF, WRF-Chem or bioaerosols is a considerable advantage but not needed for the right candidate
• Experience with PyTorch and Tensorflow in Python is an advantage, but not needed for the right candidate
Further requirements are English fluency, good writing and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and in an international academic environment.

Department of Environmental Science
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. The expertise of the department ranges from physics, chemistry, microbiology, social science, geography, economics, to policy analysis. Basic as well as applied research is conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services, and climate change. Advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other authorities. Currently, the department employs about 140 staff, postdocs and PhD students. We believe in values of equality, diversity and inclusion, and creating an attractive work/life balance. Further information can be found at www.envs.au.dk.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Section for Atmospheric Environment in the Group of Atmospheric Measurements. Due to the interdisciplinary work, be affiliated with the interdisciplinary iCLIMATE Aarhus University Interdisciplinary Centre for Climate Change (https://iclimate.au.dk/)

What we offer 
The department offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
The project offers

• A well funded research group
• Access to one of the longest pollen records in Europe for model development, collected with a Hirst trap
• Access to data from 3 Poleno Jupiters for model development. These Instrument that have been running in Denmark since 2025
• Access to DNA based observations for model development, both quantitative data and sequencing data, covering Denmark and selected European countries
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work will be at Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located approx. 30 km from Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits.

International candidates may find information concerning living and working in Denmark at www.workindenmark.dk. AU International Center offers a full range of services to make your transition to Denmark as smooth as possible (http://www.au.dk/en/internationalcentre/ias/), and the department will assist foreign candidates with finding a suitable place to live.

Contact information
Further information may be obtained by contacting Professor in Aerobiology Carsten Ambelas Skjøth (c.skjoth@envs.au.dk), https://pure.au.dk/portal/en/persons/c.skjoth@envs.au.dk or head of section Lise Lotte Sørensen (lls@envs.au.dk), https://pure.au.dk/portal/en/persons/lls@envs.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 1 November 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Help build the next generation of interactive sports experiences at Trackman.

Trackman is a global leader in sports tracking technology, trusted by professional athletes, coaches, teams, and sports organizations around the world. We are looking for a Unity Developer or Senior Unity Developer who is passionate about building high-quality interactive experiences and wants to help shape the future of our virtual sports products.

You will join a cross-functional team developing a diverse portfolio of interactive applications from family-friendly casual games and skill-based sports experiences to products supporting our growing baseball business.

The role

As a Unity Developer, you will develop and evolve products used by customers around the world. You will work across the full development lifecycle – building new features, supporting multiple platforms, improving performance and contributing to the technical architecture behind our products.

A key focus will be ABS Challenge, our interactive baseball solution supporting challenge and review situations. The product is expanding to additional platforms, including iPad and other mobile devices, and you will play an important role in creating a smooth, performant, and maintainable cross-platform experience.

At the same time, we are modernizing our software architecture across several products and teams. If you have experience with backend systems, APIs or software architecture, you will have the opportunity to contribute to these initiatives and help shape the technology foundation for future Trackman products.

Your key areas of focus

• 
Develop and evolve ABS Challenge, including expansion to new platforms.

• 
Support the development of View, part of our new software architecture.

• 
Contribute to scalable software architecture supporting future products.

What you will do

• 
Design, develop and maintain applications and features in Unity and C#.

• 
Develop our portfolio of casual games, skill-based experiences and baseball products.

• 
Bring ABS Challenge to new platforms, including iPad and other mobile devices.

• 
Optimize application performance, stability and usability across platforms.

• 
Develop tools and technical solutions that improve development workflows and team productivity.

Combilent is an entrepreneurial company specializing in the design and manufacture of high-performance solutions in the fields of Land Mobile Radio. Despite employing only 25, Combilent is the preferred supplier of components for critical communication to all the largest OEMs in US and Europe, providing premium and highly advanced components behind communication equipment to first responders such as police and alarm centrals. Being part of the Indutrade Group, a Swedish investment company with a vast network of technical companies, Combilent also benefit from their solid market presence and long-term approach to business, looking to grow organically, providing strong support to the companies in the group. Indutrade is recognized for its focus on sustainable growth and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategies, driving sustainable practices across its portfolio of businesses. We are located in Farum, north of Copenhagen and are looking for a:

Sales & Business Development Manager

Business Development – Driving New Business

Combilent has had a solid and profitable business within Land Mobile Radio (LMR) for more than 20 years, and this remains a strong foundation for the company. However, our growth ambitions go beyond LMR. We have built deep expertise and strong relationships as a niche OEM supplier of mechatronics with integrated software and Radio Frequency (RF) technology  and we now want to leverage this platform to build a second leg of business.

Therefore we target to develop an entirely new customer base of OEMs in sectors following today’s major technology trends, while leveraging our position as a niche OEM supplier.

Your job will be to bring new ideas and business opportunities, and open new doors through networking. We offer startup-up speed in combination with access to funding through our owner, and know-how to execute.

You will report to the CEO and work very closely with her and with the founder (CCO) of the company, who plays a pivotal role regarding products and customers.

Key Responsibilities – Building New Ground

In a small entrepreneurial team there will be good opportunities to shape the role, and you will, among other things, be responsible for:

• Identifying and developing new business beyond our current customer base by building relations with new OEM customers in emerging sectors such as Defense, AI, Drones and IoT and expanding into new verticals with current OEM’s through new networking.

• Generating and testing new business ideas through extensive networking outside our current contacts, translating market trends and macro shifts into concrete opportunities for the Combilent

• Building strong relationships and new networks with key customers and partners to generate leads and close new business

• Staying ahead of market trends, emerging technologies, and customer preferences to inform product development and sales strategy

• Building and presenting business cases for new products and market entries, including go-to-market strategies, and resource needs

• Playing an active role at all levels of the business, from high-level strategic discussions to hands-on sales and operational tasks, reflecting the entrepreneurial spirit of Combilent

What You Bring – A Networker and Idea-Generator

Most likely, you hold a degree in Engineering, Business, MBA or related field. You have 5+ years of experience in sales, business management and/or product development, in an industry that is tech focused. You have a hunter profile and get your energy from finding business opportunities and convert them into business. Furthermore, you are experienced in strategic thinking combined with an entrepreneurial mindset, and with the ability to thrive in a small business environment where everyone contributes.

What We Offer – Room to Build Something New

We offer a compensation package that matches your qualifications, including a pension and a bonus scheme, but just as importantly, we offer exciting professional challenges and a team that values openness and good collaboration as well as a culture, where we treat each other well. You will get a key role in a small, innovative company, providing opportunities to make a significant impact on the future direction of the company. You will get autonomy to shape and lead new business ventures, with the opportunity to influence both product development and acquisition strategies.

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Natural Product Chemistry - DTU Bioengineering
jobs.description:
Are you interested in microbial natural product research and working in a team? We have the task of charactering bioactive molecules and understanding their biosynthetic pathways. Those molecules can be further developed to help sustainable agriculture.

Responsibilities and qualifications
We are looking for an ambitious chemist with broad experience in microbial natural product chemistry and omics technologies. In this position you will have the unique opportunity to apply modern omics technologies in the investigation into bioactive natural products. The project will focus on the characterization of microbial secondary metabolites from different microbes, with the ambition to develop biofungicides. Your main analytical approach will be based on metabolomics using state-of-the-art high-resolution mass spectrometry techniques including LC/MS, MALDI imaging, NMR spectroscopy, different types of chromatography, genome-mining and microbial engineering.

This position is financed by SDC (https://sdc.university/) and you are going to carry out research collaboration with Prof. Xiujie Wang, UCAS, Beijing. In this position, you will have the unique opportunity to apply different omics technologies in natural product research.

We wish for knowledge and qualifications within

• Genome-mining and metabolomics analysis of bioactive microorganisms
• Isolation and structural elucidation of unknown and/or bioactive secondary metabolites, e.g. antifungals from microbes, using NMR and MS spectroscopy
• Biosynthesis of novel secondary metabolites using bioinformatics and genetics
• Knowledge of biofungicide
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment

• A strong background in natural product chemistry and biosynthesis
• Highly motivated by the structural complexity of microbial natural products and their applications
• Previous hands-on experience with LC-MS, MALDI-imaging and NMR is advantageous 
• Previous hands-on experience in genome-mining, biosynthesis and strain engineering is advantageous
• Previous knowledge in plant-microbe interactions is advantageous
• Strong writing and communication skills
• You are hard-working and dedicated to your work
• Interested in international collaborations
• You are a team player with a desire to work closely and help your colleagues to succeed
• Fluent in English
We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is full time for 3 years. The position starts in early 2027 and no later than 01.April 2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Ling Ding, lidi@dtu.dk 

You can read more about at https://www.bioengineering.dtu.dk/ 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• Contacts for two references
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC)
Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC) is a partnership between all eight Danish universities, the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Higher Education, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS), and the Chinese research institute Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). The overall aim of SDC is to promote and strengthen collaboration between Danish and Chinese research and education environments for the benefit of both countries. The PhD candidate is expected to spend his/her PhD external stay in Beijing Institute of Genomics, Beijing to carry out collaborations. A double degree from both DTU and UCAS will be awarded.

The Department of Biotechnology and Biomedicine (DTU Bioengineering) is an international leader in the fields of biotechnology and biomedicine. Our engineering approach to all aspects of biotechnology and biomedicine positions us as a valuable player with unique competences in a growing bio-based economy and in healthcare systems that are transforming towards personalized medicine.

We have a clear focus on the needs of the life sciences and biotech industries and contribute to innovation, new businesses, and scientific services for the benefit of society. The department has extensive collaborations with national and international research institutions and industry partners.

DTU Bioengineering has approximately 400 employees, of whom two-thirds are scientific staff. The department is located at DTU's Lyngby Campus.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Do you want to work with mechanical development — and help set the bar for what is possible in mechanical design?

Is this you?

• Are you a Senior Mechanical Engineer with a passion and flair for product development?

• Do you want to use the newest technologies to push the limits for how deep technical solutions can be scaled and applied across products, trades, and industries?

• Do you want to solve challenging mechanical problems in close collaboration with highly skilled colleagues and leading companies in the industry?

• Do you want to be part of an ambitious team and an inclusive, creative engineering community?

• Do you want to use your mind and capabilities to seek and invent superior solutions to help the industry and the green environment?

Then the job as Senior Mechanical Engineer in Component 2.0 could be the one for you!

The role

We are looking for a mechanical engineer to join our team. You will apply your knowledge of mechanical engineering, product development, and detailed design to develop mechanical components and product solutions. The position is ideal for a skilled, motivated team member who is excited about creating the most innovative mechanical solutions.

Depth is where we have our success, and depth is what we keep. We are engineers who enjoy going all the way into the fundamental mechanics and physics — and the technology around us keeps widening the capabilities. Simulation, optimisation, AI-assisted design, and fast prototyping mean that depth is no longer something time forces us to cut back on, and the depth we put into one solution can be carried on to the next. That is why we are looking for someone who is open to impact and scalability: we solve the fundamental problem rather than the single case, so one well-solved component can lift many products, customers, and industries at once. It also means we keep moving the line for what we believe is possible, and we would like you to be curious enough to help move it.

You will work in a proactive, collaborative environment that focuses on solving and creating. Development is what fills the days here — the organisation around you is built to keep it that way, so your time goes into the engineering rather than into process. We will introduce you to the newest design techniques and tools. You will be challenging what is possible to achieve in products and equipment with the lever of component design. We guarantee that you will expand your network within the industry and work with the best within their field.

What the position needs

• M.Sc. degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent

• 3+ years of experience with mechanical product development

• Strong CAD user (SolidWorks, Creo, NX or similar), and a real understanding of what the manufacturing process does to your geometry

• Proven ability to handle projects and work in a time-effective environment

• An eye for scale — for where depth in one solution can be carried on into the next

• Curiosity about the newest technologies, and a real appetite for using them to work with scalability and automation

• A dynamic, committed, and outgoing person who communicates and cooperates well

• An appreciation for working systematically, data-based, and targeted

• Proactive thinking — you would rather dig into a difficult problem than work around it

• Responsibility for actions, projects, and people

Most importantly — you are passionate about providing high quality and innovative solutions, and enthusiastic about the possibility of working together with skilled colleagues and customers to influence the future of mechanical design.

You may not tick every line above, and you do not have to. If you are strong on mechanics and production and want the rest, write anyway.

What Component 2.0 offers

• An opportunity to become part of a successful and enthusiastic development team in an informal and solution-oriented workplace

• A working day centred on development, with room to go as deep as the problem deserves

• Solutions with reach — component solutions that are adopted across many products, customers, and industries

• Competitive employment terms and benefits, good work-life balance, and influence on own tasks

• A great location in Hørsholm

• Experienced and skilled colleagues with highly diverse backgrounds

About Component 2.0

Our founding idea is to develop and provide new component solutions for generic mechanical problems in close cooperation with the industry. We believe that the right component solutions can catalyze our customers' continued work of increasing product and production performance.

Head of Technical Strategy & Growth

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position in Materials Chemistry at the Mads Clausen Institute, The University of Southern Denmark in Sønderborg, Denmark
jobs.description:
We are seeking an enthusiastic new colleague as a postdoctoral research associate in the field of Materials Chemistry with a strong background, particularly in Solid State Chemistry and (Photo)electrochemistry, and interest in industrial applications and cooperation to join the Mads Clausen Institute (MCI) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) in Sønderborg, Denmark. The position is for two years with an expected starting date of 01.03.2027. 

MCI is a part of the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) and covers research and education, including applications of engineering sciences. Our working language is English, reflecting the fact that far more than half of our students and staff have international roots. We are located at SDU’s beautiful campus in Sønderborg, in the inspiring building of Alsion, which is a centre for science, culture and learning in the heart of Sønderborg and perched on the strait of water separating the island of Als from the mainland. The university has very close relations with industries in Sønderborg, Southern Denmark, and Northern Germany.

The successful candidate is expected to carry out research mainly within a project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The project is hosted by the nanotechnology centre NanoSYD, a part of MCI, and it is integrated into the novel, active working group CatMatX, a research laboratory focused on developing next-generation catalytic materials for sustainable energy and environmental applications,  by Professor Mirabbos Hojamberdiev. The research work involves the synthesis and characterization of novel compounds based on mixed-anion compounds (e.g., transition metal (oxy)nitrides) and the evaluation of their performance in solar water splitting. Also, the successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in the supervision of MSc and PhD students affiliated with SDU NanoSYD, preparing project reports, presentations, and publications, as well as writing project proposals to support research at SDU NanoSYD. 

Job Description and Responsibilities

• 
Implementation of research tasks related to the project;

• 
Collaborative and independent research planning, materials synthesis and characterization, and evaluation of materials performance in solar water splitting;

• 
Independent characterization, data analysis, and interpretation of research results;

• 
Scientific communication and presentation of research results at group seminars, scientific conferences, project meetings, etc.;

• 
Publishing of project results in international peer-reviewed scientific journals with high impact factors.

Potential Responsibilities 

• 
Supervision of BSc, MSc, and exchange/visiting students who perform research work on similar research topics; 

• 
Assistance in teaching activities; 

• 
Assistance in setting up the research infrastructure;

• 
Assistance in the preparation of grant proposals for external funding. 

Mandatory qualifications 

• 
PhD degree in Materials Science, Materials Chemistry, Solid State Chemistry, Solid State Physics, Electrochemistry, or related fields; 

• 
Proven hands-on experience and knowledge of various synthesis methods in solid-state chemistry, preferably the methods used for the synthesis of mixed-anion compounds;

• 
Technical skills in materials characterization techniques (e.g., XRD, XPS, SEM);   

• 
Proven track record of publishing in international peer-reviewed scientific journals as leading author;

• 
Fluency in English (both spoken and written);

• 
Ability to work in teams and also independently; 

• 
Strong communication skills; 

• 
Willingness to collaborate with other scientists and industry. 

The following qualifications are advantageous

• 
Research experience in X-ray, synchrotron, and neutron radiation facilities, DFT calculations and MD simulations;

• 
Research experience in electrochemistry and solar water splitting; 

• 
Technical skills in scientific illustration and animation to deliver visual knowledge of the project; 

• 
Proven record in participating in national and international research projects;

• 
Strong interest in a long-term commitment to a growing research group.

Contact information

For more information about the department and the position, please contact Mirabbos Hojamberdiev (mirabbos@mci.sdu.dk) and Horst-Günter Rubahn (rubahn@mci.sdu.dk)

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

Conditions of employment

Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher is temporary and for an initial 2-year period, and it starts on 01.03.2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding. (no more than 4 years at the same university)

Appointment to the position will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described herein. Please check links for more information on salary (only available in Danish) and taxation.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

The assessment and evaluation process

Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. 

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

The application

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. 

To qualify for the position as postdoc you must have obtained a PhD degree by the employment date. 

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
One-page motivation letter that describes the applicant’s previous research work and experience most relevant to the offered position.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Certificates/Diplomas (Bachelor, Master, and PhD degrees) – Danish and/or English transcripts. 

• 
Complete list of publications (please highlight publications most relevant to the offered position).

• 
Research statement on developing novel transition metal-based mixed anion compounds, particularly (oxy)nitrides, for solar water splitting.

• 
A reference letter may be submitted, but is not required. 

The application and all appendices must be in English. We request files in pdf-format no more than 5 MB per file. All pdf-files must be unlocked and allow binding and may not be password protected. Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

UPLOAD GUIDE: Motivated application shall be uploaded as ‘Cover letter’, Curriculum Vitae shall be uploaded as ‘Resume’. All other documents shall be uploaded as ‘Miscellaneous documents’.

If the application does not meet the requirements mentioned above, the faculty may reject your application without further notice. Applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated.

The application deadline is October 31, 2026 at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST).

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Apply at https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu

We look forward to hearing from you!

Vetaphone is the Danish company behind the invention of corona treatment back in 1951, and for more than seven decades the family-owned business has continued to set the standard within corona and plasma surface treatment technology. From its headquarters in Kolding, Vetaphone develops advanced, reliable systems that ensure optimal adhesion, print quality and production efficiency for customers in the print, packaging, converting and extrusion industries – and today the company is represented in more than 60 countries around the world. To strengthen the international sales organisation, we are now looking for a technically strong and commercially minded:
Technical Sales ManagerTechnical and commercial sales support with close customer dialogue

As Technical Sales Manager, you become one of the key technical and commercial support behind Vetaphone’s global sales team, working closely with Area Sales Managers and agents to solve real production challenges where surface treatment performance impacts efficiency, quality and compliance. You get a broad and technically demanding role, where you guide projects from the very first customer dialogue and solution design through to quotation, negotiation and handover to the internal project department.

It is natural for you to drive technically complex, project-based sales to OEMs and end customers, and to step in as technical sales lead on selected projects in close cooperation with Area Sales Managers, agents and internal specialists. You analyse customer applications, production processes and requirements to define the optimal surface treatment solution, and you prepare and present technical and commercial proposals that communicate value, performance and compliance in a way customers understand and trust.

You support OEM customers with system integration, specification and application know-how, and build long-term customer relationships based on trust, expertise and results. At the same time, you contribute to knowledge sharing and capability building across the sales organisation and agent network, and you stay on top of market trends, customer needs and competitive developments – with regular international travel to customers, OEM partners and key industry events.

In the selection process, we will particularly emphasise:

• A solid technical background, preferably within mechanical and/or electrical engineering
• Proven experience with consultative, project-based B2B sales of technical systems or solutions
• The ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear customer value propositions
• A structured and self-driven approach, combined with strong stakeholder management skills
• Comfort working independently in an international, matrix-based organisation
• Fluent in Danish and excellent communication skills in English
• Willingness to travel internationally approx. 50-70 days per year
The ideal candidate has a solid technical foundation combined with a genuine sales flair, and thrives in a role where every project brings a new technical puzzle to solve. Maybe you already work in a similar technical sales role today, or you come from an engineering or application background and are ready to take the step into a more commercial, customer-facing career.

In return, you become part of a global technology leader with a strong market position, working closely with experienced technical and commercial colleagues on high-value international projects – with good opportunities for professional development within a specialised, knowledge-driven organisation.

The role is based at Vetaphone’s headquarters in Kolding, Denmark, combined with the international travel the role calls for.

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Selectors® Partner Lars Mikkelsen at 2219 4930 or Selectors® on 7210 0030.
